subject: Urban Planning
title: Community Land Trusts
description: A quick win: understand Community Land Trusts.

hook.text: What if the community owned the land and you only owned the house? That's a community land trust.

buildup.text: CLTs buy land and hold it permanently. Homeowners purchase the building but lease the land at low cost.

discovery.text: When owners sell, resale prices are capped. The home stays affordable for the next buyer, forever.

twist.text: During the 2008 crash, CLT homeowners defaulted at one-tenth the rate of conventional mortgage holders.

climax.text: Burlington, Vermont's CLT, founded in 1984, now manages over 3,000 permanently affordable housing units.

punchline.text: Own the home. Share the land. Keep it affordable forever.

quiz.question: How do community land trusts maintain long-term housing affordability?
options: Government subsidies cover the gap between market and affordable rents each year
The trust owns the land permanently and caps resale prices on homes built on it
Residents contribute volunteer labor instead of paying property taxes
